Earth has a mean density of about \(5.5\ \text{g/cm}^3\), so planets (a) and (b) have essentially the same density.

For planets with Earth-like composition, greater mass produces stronger gravitational compression. Thus, a 5-Earth-mass planet (c) would have a higher mean density than Earth, while a half-Earth-mass planet (d) would be less compressed and therefore less dense.

Answer: c
